title: Chardonnay around the world
subtitle: From Chablis to California
objectives: Name Chardonnay's classic regions in Burgundy
Compare cool and warm climate Chardonnay
Recognise the effect of oak and malolactic

steps.title: Burgundy, the template
steps.body: Chardonnay comes from Burgundy, where it makes almost all the white wine. Chablis, in the cool north, gives lean, steely wines with green apple and lemon, often unoaked. The Côte de Beaune, with Meursault and Puligny-Montrachet, gives richer, nutty wines fermented and aged in oak. The Mâconnais, further south, gives rounder, fruitier, good-value wines.
steps.highlight: Chablis: steely. Côte de Beaune: rich.

steps.title: Beyond Burgundy
steps.body: Chardonnay grows almost everywhere. In warm places like California's Central Valley or parts of Australia it gives tropical fruit, high alcohol and often lots of oak. Cooler sites, like Sonoma Coast, Tasmania, Adelaide Hills or Limarí in Chile, now make tighter, fresher styles. Since the 2000s, many producers have cut back on new oak and malolactic.
steps.highlight: Cool sites: citrus. Warm sites: tropical.

steps.prompt: Which Burgundy area is known for lean, steely, often unoaked Chardonnay?
steps.explanation: Chablis is the coolest part of Burgundy, and its wines are typically crisp and mineral. Meursault is richer and oaked.

steps.title: The winemaker's touch
steps.body: Chardonnay takes winemaking well. Barrel fermentation and new oak add vanilla and toast. Malolactic conversion turns sharp malic acid into soft lactic acid, adding a buttery note. Lees stirring gives a creamy texture. Unoaked versions are fresh and fruity. The label rarely tells you which, but the region and price are good clues.
steps.highlight: Oak, malolactic and lees shape the style

steps.prompt: Which flavours suggest a warm-climate, oaked Chardonnay?
steps.explanation: Tropical fruit comes from heat; vanilla, toast and butter from oak and malolactic. Green apple and lime point to a cool climate.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Burgundy is Chardonnay's home: Chablis lean, the Côte de Beaune rich
Cool sites give citrus; warm sites give tropical fruit
Oak, malolactic and lees add toast, butter and cream
